question: o04
q: How many people tapped on at Central station last Friday?

transcript.answer:
I can't give you that number. My data doesn't include tap-ons for individual stations or single days, so there's no count for Central on Friday 16 October 2026.

The closest source is TfNSW Opal tap data (via Commute Pulse). It only covers six commercial centres: Sydney CBD, North Sydney, Chatswood, Macquarie Park, Strathfield and Parramatta. It counts afternoon and evening tap-ons (3pm–7pm), and the data is monthly, not daily. The latest month is **September 2026**, so nothing for October yet.

What it does show is how quiet Fridays are in the **Sydney CBD**. This is Friday evening tap-ons as a share of the Tuesday–Thursday average:

| Month (2026) | Friday vs midweek |
|---|---|
| Jan | 0.744 |
| Apr | 0.797 |
| Aug | 0.799 (highest this year) |
| **Sep (latest)** | **0.783** |

So in September 2026, about **22% fewer** people tapped on in the CBD on a Friday evening than on a typical midweek evening. The gap has narrowed a bit since January, when it was about 26%. One caveat: it's unclear whether Sydney Metro taps are included.

For Central on a specific day, try the station-level files on the TfNSW Open Data Hub ("Opal Patronage"). They're usually published with a lag, so last Friday's figures may not be there yet. I can also pull the CBD's average Tuesday–Thursday evening tap-ons, or compare the Friday gap with Parramatta or North Sydney.
